name: Primary open-angle glaucoma
summary: Chronic optic neuropathy: the cup enlarges, the rim thins and notches, with disc haemorrhages and nerve-fibre loss; the front of the eye looks normal.

revealed_by.fundus: Through the 90D lens: a large vertically oval cup, the inferior rim thinner than the superior (ISNT broken), an inferotemporal notch, a splinter haemorrhage at the disc margin, peripapillary atrophy; in advanced disease a pale disc with almost no rim.
revealed_by.tonometry: IOP often above 21 mmHg, but normal-tension glaucoma is common.

teaching_points: Judge the rim, not just the cup: follow the ISNT rule and look for a notch.
A disc haemorrhage is a sign of progression.
A large disc has a large cup: relate the cup to the disc size before calling glaucoma.

provenance.source: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology, 9th ed.; EGS Terminology and Guidelines for Glaucoma, 5th ed.; Jonas et al., Surv Ophthalmol 43:293 (1999) for cup and rim changes
